comment: Every hand-written scope inside scripts/ci, with the reason it is not derived.
scripts/ci/check_scan_scope.py is the only reader. A scope list that can be
derived from its subject must be derived instead of registered here; an entry
is a statement that the subject genuinely has no machine-readable extent -- a
frozen historical inventory, a taxonomy that assigns meaning rather than
membership, or a named authority whose identity is the rule.
Both sections are complete and ratcheted: a new member of either subject set
fails the gate, and an entry naming something that no longer exists fails too,
so the baselines only go down.

_realization_permit_fitness.py.reason: a helper module imported by check_crate_boundaries.py, whose __main__ exists only for running the fitness function standalone; its inputs are the importer's

_session_effect_fitness.py.reason: a helper module imported by check_crate_boundaries.py, whose __main__ exists only for running the fitness function standalone; its inputs are the importer's

check_authority_arithmetic.py.reason: runs inside the rust shell gate, which owns one hand-written trigger for every checker it invokes rather than one trigger per checker

check_crate_boundaries.py.reason: runs inside the rust shell gate, which owns one hand-written trigger for every checker it invokes rather than one trigger per checker

check_degrading_defaults.py.reason: runs only in the static group of the full gate; it has no pre-commit command, so there is no trigger for a declaration to render

check_dependency_gates.py.reason: runs only in the static group of the full gate; it has no pre-commit command, so there is no trigger for a declaration to render

check_dependency_sources.py.reason: runs inside the rust shell gate, which owns one hand-written trigger for every checker it invokes rather than one trigger per checker

check_feature_matrix.py.reason: runs inside the rust shell gate, which owns one hand-written trigger for every checker it invokes rather than one trigger per checker

check_formal_mutations.py.reason: runs inside the formal gate, which is scheduled rather than file-triggered because a proof run costs minutes, not milliseconds

check_formal_web_surface.py.reason: runs inside the formal gate, which is scheduled rather than file-triggered because a proof run costs minutes, not milliseconds

check_managed_wire_naming.py.reason: has a pre-commit command whose glob is still hand-written; declaring inputs here belongs with the hook-hygiene work, not with this scope change

check_node_dependencies.py.reason: has a pre-commit command whose glob is still hand-written; declaring inputs here belongs with the hook-hygiene work, not with this scope change

check_product_release.py.reason: runs only in the docs group of the full gate; it has no pre-commit command, so there is no trigger for a declaration to render

check_test_orchestration.py.reason: has a pre-commit command whose glob is still hand-written, and the module is being changed in another lane, so its declaration is deferred rather than raced

export_homogeneous_lcov.py.reason: a coverage export tool rather than a gate: it reads profraw output produced by the run that invokes it, not a set of repository files

formal_run_evidence.py.reason: an evidence writer rather than a gate: it walks the artefact directory the proof run just produced, which is not a repository input at all

render_runtime_refinement_traces.py.reason: a renderer rather than a gate: it walks the trace directory the reliability run just produced, which is not a repository input at all

test_bootstrap_kani.py.reason: a self-test of the solver bootstrap; it walks the temporary trees its own fixtures build, so it has no repository input set to declare

test_formal_run_evidence.py.reason: a self-test whose corpus is the dependency closure of the entry scripts it copies, derived at run time rather than declared

test_postgres_recovery_root.py.reason: a self-test of the recovery drill; it walks the temporary trees its own fixtures build, so it has no repository input set to declare

_coordinator_authority_fitness.py:ATTEMP.reason: the five dispatch-attempt backends are named authorities; a walk of run-ingress would also collect the ports and adapters that must not implement the arithmetic

_execution_ownership_fitness.py:PUBLIC_R.reason: these are the discovery roots that make the inventory above complete; they name which trees serve public ingress, which no file in those trees states about itself

_execution_ownership_fitness.py:RAW_TOOL.reason: the three crates permitted to hold a raw tool registry are a stated exception list; deriving it from who holds one would make the rule agree with whatever exists

_execution_ownership_fitness.py:ROUTE_OW.reason: the inventory is already paired with a discovery walk over PUBLIC_ROUTE_ROOTS, which is the completeness assertion: a new router source cannot escape it silently

_migration_fitness.py:PUBLISHED_LEGACY_C.reason: the exact per-owner counts those frozen receipts are allowed to declare; a count cannot be derived from the code it is meant to pin

_migration_fitness.py:PUBLISHED_LEGACY_S.reason: frozen receipts of migrations already published to operators; a closed historical inventory that must never grow, so derivation from the tree would defeat its purpose

_realization_permit_fitness.py:LOCAL_REA.reason: the one owner, one re-export and one composition-root field of the registry type; a second holder is a second exclusion and must fail, not be discovered

_realization_permit_fitness.py:REALIZATI.reason: the two permitted entry points into the phase driver, each paired with the accessor it must take its permit from; a walk would admit any new caller
the two exclusion identity sources are the rule itself: a third minter is the defect, so the set cannot be read back from whoever mints one

_resource_plane_fitness.py:MEMORY_STORE_.reason: the two driving adapters allowed to read memory-store identity through the port; a third would be discovered rather than refused if this were derived

_resource_plane_fitness.py:RESOURCE_APPL.reason: resource adapters living inside mixed-role crates, whose owning crate is legitimately broader; nothing in the tree distinguishes them from their siblings

_resource_plane_fitness.py:RESOURCE_HTTP.reason: the HTTP handlers that must extract the workspace stamp; membership is an architectural role, not a directory, and the surrounding crate holds both kinds

_service_data_ownership_fitness.py:CREDE.reason: the three modules permitted to refresh a credential; the rule exists precisely so a fourth cannot be added by writing one

_session_state_ownership_fitness.py:SESS.reason: the three crate roots allowed to mutate session state; which trees may is an ownership decision no file in them declares about itself

_sqlite_scheduler_fitness.py:ASYNC_SQLIT.reason: the two adapters that drive sqlite from async code and therefore need the scheduler rule; a third is the defect the rule is written to catch

check_authority_arithmetic.py:RULES.reason: each entry pairs an authority file with the arithmetic it must not re-derive, so the list carries the rule and not merely the scope

check_degrading_defaults.py:FAIL_OPEN_RE.reason: the frozen inventory of fail-open reads this ratchet is driving to zero; a walk would recompute today's count and so could never detect a new one
each entry is a read whose default was argued to be correct in review; membership is a judgement about that call site, not a property any walk of the tree can observe

check_dependency_gates.py:SILENT_SKIP_EX.reason: two files whose short-circuit on an absent dependency is sound; soundness is a judgement about the test, not a property any walk can read

check_fabricated_facts.py:COMPOSITION_RO.reason: a composition root is where the process is allowed to read the wall clock; nothing in those files declares that status, and inferring it from a binary target would admit every test harness

check_file_limits.py:CODE_SUFFIXES.reason: a taxonomy, not a scope: the suffix decides which line budget applies, and no directory walk can say whether a new extension is code, doc or config

check_file_limits.py:CONFIG_SUFFIXES.reason: same taxonomy: these suffixes select the configuration budget, which nothing in the repository tree states about a file

check_file_limits.py:DOC_SUFFIXES.reason: same taxonomy: these suffixes select the documentation budget rather than the code one, which is a decision and not a discoverable fact

check_gate_arguments.py:ADDITIONAL_ENTRY.reason: gate entry points outside scripts/ci that no directory walk of that tree can reach; they are named by the lanes that run them, not by their own location

check_gate_arguments.py:ENTRY_POINT_EXEM.reason: transparent argument passthroughs (kani.sh execs cargo kani "$@"); refusing an unknown flag there would refuse the tool's own flags, which is a property of the wrapper's contract, not of its text

check_lane_reachability.py:UNSELECTED_EX.reason: executables no lane runs today, each recorded with what covers the behaviour instead; a walk cannot distinguish a deliberate manual drill from a script that was orphaned by accident

check_observation_collapse.py:TRANSLATED.reason: three dispatch-transport declarations that keep Result<Option<StreamCheckpoint>> because one named file translates it into the tri-state; the checker verifies that translation still exists and that each file still carries the shape, so the list cannot outlive its reason

check_reliability.py:REQUIRED_SURFACES.reason: an inventory of surfaces that must exist; deriving it from the tree would make the rule agree with whatever is present and assert nothing

check_repository_hygiene.py:DOC_NAME_EXC.reason: three documents allowed to carry an otherwise forbidden name; each is a decision someone made and can be argued with, not a discoverable property

check_repository_hygiene.py:GENERATED_SU.reason: a taxonomy of generated artefacts that may never be committed; being generated is not something the file itself records

check_repository_hygiene.py:TEXT_SUFFIXE.reason: a taxonomy selecting which files the text hygiene rules can read at all; a walk cannot tell text from binary by extension without this judgement

check_secrets.py:CODE_SUFFIXES.reason: the module already scans every staged file by declaring INPUT_GLOBS ('**/*'); this taxonomy only chooses which of them get the code-shaped secret rules

check_test_orchestration.py:SECONDARY_RU.reason: the two coverage runners allowed beside the deterministic one; a third runner is the drift the rule exists to refuse, so it may not be discovered

check_test_orchestration.py:STORE_BACKEN.reason: the four store backends whose conformance suite must be wired; derivable from a crate walk, but this module is being changed in another lane, so it is registered rather than edited here
